title: The Scream
source: National Museum, Oslo (public domain: Munch died in 1944). Full resolution of the 1893 painted version from Wikimedia Commons: Edvard_Munch,_1893,_The_Scream,_oil,_tempera_and_pastel_on_cardboard,_91_x_73_cm,_National_Gallery_of_Norway.jpg
caption: Everyone thinks the figure is screaming. It isn't. And someone wrote a tiny message in the sky. #art #arthistory #painting #history #oilpainting

slides.headline: Hands over his ears
slides.text: The figure is not screaming, he is hearing a scream. Munch wrote that he felt an endless scream passing through nature.

slides.headline: A real sunset
slides.text: Munch described walking with two friends at sunset when the sky suddenly turned blood red, and he stopped, shaking with fear.

slides.headline: His two friends
slides.text: Behind him, two figures keep walking calmly. They don't feel anything. He is alone with what he feels.

slides.headline: A message in the sky
slides.text: In the red sky there is a tiny pencil inscription: "Can only have been painted by a madman." For years no one knew who wrote it.

slides.headline: It was Munch
slides.text: In 2021 the National Museum in Oslo confirmed the handwriting is Munch's own. He may have written it after critics questioned his mental health.

slides.headline: A real place
slides.text: The road, the railing and the fjord are a real view from a hill above Oslo. You can still stand there today.

slides.headline: Why so red?
slides.text: Some think the sky recalls sunsets after the 1883 Krakatoa eruption, others rare mother-of-pearl clouds. Or simply how it felt.

slides.headline: Stolen twice
slides.text: Munch made several versions. Two of them were stolen, in 1994 and 2004. Both were recovered.
